description:
NEW MODULE: OctoPi.Coder.Extension.Manager (GenServer)
FILES: new extension/manager.ex, dispatcher.ex, session supervisor startup

This ticket establishes Extension.Manager, the per-session process that owns the complete extension stack for one agent instance. It replaces the vague 'TableOwner' concept and is the answer to session isolation: each session gets its own Manager, its own extensions, its own state.

WHAT EXTENSION.MANAGER DOES:
1. Loads extensions on init (calls Loader.load_all/1 with the session's configured extension paths).
2. For each loaded Extension.t() that has a state_agent pid (set by the macro in opi-fin.2.2): records the pid for lifecycle management.
3. Creates and owns three ETS tables:
   - :bag   {event_type, ext_id, handler_fn}  -- handler dispatch (read_concurrency: true)
   - :set   {tool_name, tool_def}              -- tool lookup (read_concurrency: true)
   - :set   {flag_name, flag_value}            -- flag reads (read_concurrency: true)
   Tables are :protected and session-scoped (NOT global atom names).
4. Populates all three tables from the loaded [Extension.t()] list.
5. Holds the [Extension.t()] list for introspection queries (get_all_commands, get_all_flags, etc.).
6. In terminate/2: stops all state Agents collected in step 2. Tables die automatically when the process exits.

WHY PER-SESSION ISOLATION WORKS:
Each session's Extension.Manager loads its own extension instances. Two concurrent sessions running the same extension code have separate Extension.t() structs, separate Agent pids, and separate ETS tables. ctx.host, ctx.ui, and ETS table refs in Context are all session-scoped. Extensions do not need to know which session they are in.

SUPERVISION: Extension.Manager is started as a child of Session.Supervisor (see opi-fin.6.2 for the full session supervision tree). It is started before Session.Runner so tables are ready when the Runner begins dispatching.

start_link opts: %{extension_paths: [...], extension_factories: [...]}
Public API:
  Extension.Manager.table_refs(pid) -> %{handlers: tid, tools: tid, flags: tid}
  Extension.Manager.extensions(pid) -> [Extension.t()]

DISPATCHER CHANGE: Dispatcher.all_handlers/2 currently takes [Extension.t()] and scans. Change to accept a handlers ETS table tid. The tid reaches Dispatcher via Context -- add a handlers_table: :ets.tid() field to Context.t(). Session.Runner populates it from Extension.Manager.table_refs before each dispatch.

Extension.t() structs are still built identically -- ETS is populated FROM them. Introspection functions (get_all_tools, get_all_commands, etc.) query Extension.Manager.extensions/1 for the list, unchanged.

TEST: New extension/manager_test.exs. Test: (1) loads extensions and populates tables; (2) two Manager instances started with the same extension paths have independent tables and independent Agent pids; (3) terminate/2 stops all Agents; (4) Dispatcher.emit reads from the table and calls the right handlers.
title: ETS handler dispatch table
